questions.question: Describe a time you used data to identify the real cause of an operational problem rather than treating its visible symptom. What data did you examine, what did you conclude, and what changed?

Walk me through how you would turn a broad request such as “improve mobile service onboarding” into a set of validated business requirements, including the people you would involve and the artifacts you would produce.
Give an example of a commitment you owned from initial issue through completion. How did you track actions, manage risks or blockers, and confirm the intended result was achieved?
What sections would you include in a detailed analysis report for leadership after reviewing a process, and how would you make the recommendations traceable to the underlying evidence?
Tell me about a time you had to gain support for a process change from people who initially preferred the existing way of working. How did you tailor your case, and what was the outcome?
What would you include in a business case for automating a manual process, and how would you evaluate whether automation is preferable to improving the existing workflow?
A business sponsor says a mobile feature is “too slow,” while the technical team asks for measurable acceptance criteria. How would you frame the problem and translate it into testable requirements?
In a mobile-process review, operations, technology, and management stakeholders want different outcomes. How would you run the discussion to surface trade-offs and reach an acceptable solution?
When documenting requirements, how do you distinguish business requirements, functional requirements, nonfunctional requirements, assumptions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria?
Tell me about a system issue you investigated involving NALCOMIS, SYBASE, or Windows NT. How did you isolate the issue, coordinate resolution, and verify that normal operations had been restored?
